penurious

puh-NYUR-ee-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Penurious is extremely stingy, especially despite having enough money to spend.

The landlord was so penurious that he refused to call a plumber, patching the leaking pipe himself with tape.

Example

The company's penurious founder still photocopied both sides of every page to save paper, even after the business went public.

Photocopying both sides of every page to save paper, even after going public, is exactly the extreme, joyless stinginess penurious describes.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

penny-pinching: Penny-pinching is fretting over the smallest sums -- hunting coupons, grumbling over a dime -- and it is often mild, even affectionate. Penurious is harsher and stranger: extreme, joyless stinginess that shocks people precisely because the penurious person could easily afford to spend.

tightfisted: Tightfisted means reluctant to part with money -- slow to reach for a wallet, quick to skip a tip. Penurious pushes that reluctance into an extreme that rules a whole life, and it stings more because the penurious person has plenty to spend.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

generous: willing to give or spend freely

Where it sits · how tightly money is held onto

sparing → penurious → avaricious

sparing vs. penurious: Being sparing simply means spending carefully to avoid waste -- a mild, sensible habit; penurious pushes that same instinct into extreme, joyless stinginess.

avaricious vs. penurious: Avaricious pushes further than penurious: a penurious person grimly refuses to release the money they have, while an avaricious one clutches every coin and hungers to pile up more.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together: Penurious traces to Latin penuria, 'want, need, scarcity' -- describing someone who acts as though scarcity is always just around the corner, even when it isn't.

Use the root in a new word: penury: Penurious grows from Latin penuria, and the same root gives the rarer noun penury — a word you will mostly meet in older books. Penurious describes penny-pinching behavior; a penurious person can act that way while sitting on a full bank account.

Word Building

Word Choice

Penurious focuses on stinginess as a behavior, often surprising precisely because the person could easily afford to spend. It is a close relative of "impecunious" (taught earlier in this course), which instead describes someone who genuinely has no money at all -- "impecunious" is about lacking funds; Penurious is about refusing to use funds one has.
